what iconic world landmark, sometimes ca: Times Square in New York City was called Longacre Square until 1904, when the New York Times moved its headquarters there and the area was renamed. It is nicknamed the "Crossroads of the World".
which medieval monument is an essential: The Palace of the Grand Master was built by the Knights Hospitaller, a medieval order of crusading knights who ruled Rhodes from 1309 to 1522. It sits inside the walled Old Town, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
what was the original height of the grea: The Great Pyramid was originally about 481 feet (146.6 m) high, but it has lost its smooth outer casing stones, so it is now around 455 feet. It was the tallest man-made structure for nearly 4,000 years.
what is the estimated frame of time in w: The Great Pyramid is believed to have been built in roughly 15 to 20 years, during the reign of Pharaoh Khufu around 2560 BC. That's an astonishing pace, given that it used more than 2 million stone blocks.
what is the length of the entire great w: The "5,500 miles" figure is the commonly quoted length of the Great Wall of China including its branches. A later Chinese survey counted all wall sections from many dynasties and arrived at a much larger total of about 13,000 miles.
the name, chargoggagoggmanchauggauggagog: That long name belongs to a lake in Webster, Massachusetts, often called Lake Webster. The name comes from a Native American word that is said to roughly mean a fishing place at the boundaries, a neutral meeting ground.
the cable cars of this city are the only: San Francisco's cable cars are the only moving National Historic Landmark in the United States. The system has operated since 1873 and still uses a cable running under the street.
the great pyramid of giza, the oldest of: The Great Pyramid of Giza was built around 4,500 years ago and is the oldest of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World. It's the only one of those wonders that still largely stands today.
the statue of liberty, is one of the mos: The Statue of Liberty stands on Liberty Island in New York Harbor in the United States. It was a gift from France, dedicated in 1886, designed by Frédéric Auguste Bartholdi, and its iron framework was engineered by Gustave Eiffel.
which tower, located in the palace of we: "Big Ben" is actually the nickname of the Great Bell inside the tower, not the tower itself. The tower, called the Clock Tower, was renamed the Elizabeth Tower in 2012 for Queen Elizabeth II's Diamond Jubilee.
the design of which japanese tower is ba: Tokyo Tower, completed in 1958, was modeled on the Eiffel Tower, but it's taller at 333 meters, compared with the Eiffel Tower's roughly 330 meters. It's painted white and international orange to meet aviation safety rules.
which of the following is a tall tower i: The Sky Tower in Auckland, New Zealand, is 328 meters tall and opened in 1997. It's the tallest free-standing structure in the Southern Hemisphere and has a viewing deck and a bungee-like jump.
which australian tower was previously kn: Sydney Tower, formerly called Centrepoint Tower, is 309 meters tall and opened in 1981. It is the tallest observation tower in Sydney and in the Southern Hemisphere's biggest city.
how old is the great wall of china?: Parts of the Great Wall date back more than 2,000 years, to the time of China's first emperor, Qin Shi Huang, around 221 BC. The best-known stone and brick sections were built much later, during the Ming dynasty.
in what direction does the tower of pisa: The Leaning Tower of Pisa leans toward the southeast, and it began sinking soon after construction started because it was built on soft soil. Engineers reduced the tilt in the 1990s and 2000s, so it is now stable.
approximately how high is the tower of p: The Leaning Tower of Pisa is about 56 meters (183 feet) tall on its low side. Because it leans, the highest side is a bit taller than the lowest.
which country is home to the huge and sp: Christ the Redeemer stands on Corcovado mountain in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. Completed in 1931, the 30-meter-tall statue is one of the New Seven Wonders of the World.
how many workers were recruited to build: About 20,000 workers, including masons, carvers and craftsmen from across Asia, built the Taj Mahal over roughly two decades, from 1632 to 1653. Mughal emperor Shah Jahan commissioned it as a tomb for his wife Mumtaz Mahal.
attila the huns palace and headquarters: Attila the Hun's capital is believed to have been on the Great Hungarian Plain, between the Danube and Tisza rivers, in what is now Hungary. The exact site has never been found.
which peculiarity of the great pyramid i: Unlike other pyramids, whose chambers are mostly underground or at ground level, the Great Pyramid has a Grand Gallery and upper chambers that sit high inside the structure. These ascending passages lead to the King's Chamber.
when helen keller passed away, in what c: Helen Keller died in 1968, and her ashes were placed at the Washington National Cathedral, next to those of her teacher, Anne Sullivan. She was deaf and blind, and she became a famous author and activist.
what is the oldest cathedral in germany?: Trier Cathedral, in Germany's oldest city, is the country's oldest cathedral, and it sits on a site first built in the 4th century. Emperor Constantine's mother, Helena, is linked to its early history.
the statue of zeus, a wonder of the anci: The Statue of Zeus at Olympia was made of ivory plates and gold over a wooden frame, a style called chryselephantine. It was about 12 meters tall and showed Zeus seated on a throne.
this city is situated at the foot of the: Tehran, Iran's capital, lies at the foot of the Alborz mountains, and the Azadi Tower, completed in 1971, is its best-known symbol. It was originally called the Shahyad Tower.
where was the great statue of zeus locat: The Statue of Zeus was located in the Temple of Zeus at Olympia, Greece, the site of the ancient Olympic Games. The statue was lost, probably destroyed in a fire in late antiquity.
buckingham palace, the official home of: The original Buckingham House was built in 1703 for the Duke of Buckingham, and the British royal family later turned it into a palace. It's the monarch's official London residence, which since 2022 means King Charles III.
the design of this london monument, situ: Marble Arch was designed by John Nash in the 1820s after the Arch of Constantine in Rome. It originally stood in front of Buckingham Palace before being moved to its current site near Speakers' Corner in 1851.
brussels' famous comedic statue, manneke: Jeanneke Pis is a small statue of a girl squatting, in Brussels, put up in 1987 as a counterpart to the Manneken Pis. Both are in the Belgian capital's old city.
the leaning tower of pisa is actually a: The Leaning Tower of Pisa is the bell tower (campanile) of Pisa Cathedral, and it holds seven bells, one for each note of the musical major scale. Galileo is said to have used the tower for experiments with falling objects.
this tv tower in shanghai, china, was de: The Oriental Pearl Tower, completed in 1994, has spheres inspired by a Tang dynasty poem about pearls falling onto a jade plate. It's 468 meters tall and a symbol of modern Shanghai.
which 350-meter tower in las vegas, neva: The Stratosphere Tower, now called the STRAT, stands 350 meters (1,149 ft) tall on the Las Vegas Strip. It has thrill rides on top, and it's the tallest observation tower in the United States.
what is the name of the tower that was b: Liberation Tower in Kuwait City began construction in 1987, and its work was interrupted by the Iraqi invasion in 1990. After Kuwait was liberated in 1991, it was renamed and later completed in 1996.
what was the main reason for constructin: The Great Wall was built to defend against raids by nomadic groups from the north, and it also helped control borders and trade routes. It was built and rebuilt by many Chinese dynasties over centuries.
about how many years did the tower of pi: The Leaning Tower of Pisa took almost 200 years to complete, from 1173 to 1372, because construction was interrupted by wars and by the building's sinking. Builders waited for the soil to settle, which may have kept it from falling.
this landmark built by constantine the g: The Church of the Nativity in Bethlehem stands over the site traditionally believed to be Jesus's birthplace. The first church was commissioned by Constantine the Great and completed around 339 AD.
this simple farm house at the seaside wa: The Royal Pavilion in Brighton, England, began as a modest farmhouse and was turned into a lavish palace by the architect John Nash for the Prince Regent, later George IV. Its design is Indian-inspired, with onion domes.
what is the name of the landmark office: The Renaissance Center, with its cluster of towers on the Detroit riverfront, has served as General Motors' world headquarters since 1996. It was originally built in the 1970s as a revitalization project.
what landmark is known in the egyptian l: Luxor Temple, on the east bank of the Nile in Egypt, was known to the ancient Egyptians as ipet resyt, "the southern sanctuary". It was linked to nearby Karnak by an avenue of sphinxes.
what landmark near islamic cairo was hom: The Citadel of Saladin in Cairo, begun in 1176 by Saladin, was the seat of Egypt's rulers for about 700 years. It stands on a hill overlooking Cairo's Islamic district.
in what palace is the famous sistine cha: The Sistine Chapel is in the Apostolic Palace in Vatican City, the pope's official residence. Michelangelo painted its famous ceiling between 1508 and 1512.
which landmark in greece is also known a: The Acropolis of Athens was once known as Cecropia, after the legendary first king of Athens, Cecrops. The Parthenon, built in the 5th century BC, is its most famous building.
upon completion, the washington monument: Robert Mills designed the Washington Monument, a 555-foot obelisk completed in 1884. It was the tallest structure in the world until the Eiffel Tower surpassed it in 1889.
the great pyramid of giza claimed to be: The Great Pyramid stands on the Giza plateau, on the west bank of the Nile near Cairo. It remained the world's tallest man-made structure until the 14th century, when Lincoln Cathedral in England surpassed it.
what large art deco statue has become an: Christ the Redeemer, an Art Deco statue completed in 1931, towers above Rio de Janeiro from the top of Corcovado mountain. It was designed by French sculptor Paul Landowski and Brazilian engineer Heitor da Silva Costa.
in what spanish city is the alhambra pal: The Alhambra is a hilltop palace-fortress in Granada, in southern Spain. It was built mostly in the 13th and 14th centuries by the Nasrid rulers, the last Muslim dynasty in Spain.
the monument called the egg, located in: The "Egg of Columbus" monument in Sant Antoni de Portmany, Ibiza, honors Christopher Columbus. Its egg shape refers to the story of Columbus standing an egg on its end to prove a point.
how tall is chicago's sears tower?: Chicago's Sears Tower, now the Willis Tower, is 1,451 feet (442 meters) tall to its roof, and about 1,729 feet with its antennas. It was the world's tallest building from 1974 to 1998.
the wedding ceremony of charles, prince: Prince Charles and Lady Diana Spencer married at St Paul's Cathedral in London on July 29, 1981, in front of a TV audience of millions. The cathedral, designed by Christopher Wren, is the seat of the Bishop of London.
which classical greek sculptor designed: The Greek sculptor Phidias created the Statue of Zeus at Olympia, and he also oversaw the sculptures of the Parthenon in Athens. His statues are among the most admired works of ancient Greece.
following his idea of strong italy, this: In the 1930s, Benito Mussolini's government poured concrete into the foundations of the Leaning Tower of Pisa in an effort to straighten it, but this actually made the tilt worse. Engineers solved the problem only decades later.
which tall tower in malaysia, built in 1: Menara Kuala Lumpur (KL Tower), completed in 1995, stands 421 meters tall and hosts the annual "Tower Run", a race up its 2,058 steps. It is used for telecommunications as well as sightseeing.
which famous moscow tv and radio tower w: The Ostankino Tower, designed by Nikolai Nikitin and completed in 1967, is a 540-meter TV and radio tower in Moscow. It was the tallest free-standing structure in the world until 1975.
what palace is known as the official res: The Palácio da Alvorada, designed by Oscar Niemeyer, is the official residence of Brazil's president in the capital, Brasília. It was completed in 1958 and is known for its elegant curved columns.
where in st petersburg can you find the: The Bronze Horseman, a statue of Peter the Great on a rearing horse, stands in Senate Square (also called Decembrists' Square) in Saint Petersburg, near the Admiralty. Catherine the Great commissioned it, and Pushkin wrote a famous poem about it.
this statue, which was enshrined in 2005: The Guanyin of the South Sea of Sanya stands about 108 meters tall on Hainan Island, China, and was consecrated in 2005. It depicts the Buddhist goddess of mercy.
the great pyramid is one of the pyramids: The Giza complex has the pyramids of Khufu, Khafre and Menkaure, plus the Great Sphinx. The Pyramid of Amenemhat I is at Lisht, far to the south, and isn't part of it.
who ordered the construction of dolmabah: Sultan Abdülmecid I ordered the Dolmabahçe Palace, built between 1843 and 1856 on the Bosphorus in Istanbul. It's a blend of Ottoman and European architecture and replaced the Topkapı Palace as the sultans' main residence.
this massive step pyramid (about 210 by: The Ziggurat of Ur, in what is now Iraq, was built around 2100 BC by King Ur-Nammu. It's the best preserved ziggurat, a stepped temple-tower, from ancient Sumer.
this building inspired the biblical myth: The Etemenanki, a ziggurat dedicated to Marduk in ancient Babylon, is widely believed to have inspired the Biblical story of the Tower of Babel. Little of it survives today.
what is the name of the tall tower in ro: The Euromast in Rotterdam was built in 1960 for the Floriade garden festival and is about 185 meters tall including a later extension. It's among the best-known landmarks of the Dutch port city.
this building, designed by louis h. sull: The Carson Pirie Scott building in Chicago, designed by Louis Sullivan, is famous for its ornate iron decoration at the entrance. It appears in Theodore Dreiser's 1900 novel Sister Carrie and is now known as the Sullivan Center.
mustafa kemal atatürk, the first preside: Mustafa Kemal Atatürk, founder of modern Turkey, used Dolmabahçe Palace as his presidential residence in Istanbul and died there in 1938. The palace clocks are set to the time of his death, 9:05.
